title: Measuring Timing, Latency and Resource Use

contract.reader: A firmware developer who has done or read a schedulability analysis and must obtain its inputs and check its outcomes on real hardware
contract.problem: Measuring execution time, response time, latency, jitter, processor load and memory use correctly, and knowing how far a measured maximum can be trusted as a worst case
contract.outcome: Choose an instrument (GPIO and logic analyzer, cycle counter, trace); keep wrap-safe high-water marks; explain why the observed maximum is not the WCET and quantify the risk; feed measured values with a margin into RTA; report latency as a distribution; measure load with an idle counter and stack use by painting; run the verification cycle on every build
contract.contribution: Measurement as the closing half of the analysis of entry 4: the (1 - p)^n argument for missed rare paths, a worked feedback of measured times into RTA, an absolute-versus-relative sleeping drift experiment and small runnable demonstrations
contract.evidence: One Python script and three C programs with real output (the deterministic ones re-run in the live review); Arm DDI 0403E.e, IEEE Std 1003.1-2017, Wilhelm et al. (2008), Buttazzo (2011), Lee and Seshia (2017), White (2011), Yiu (2014)
contract.limitations: The jitter experiment runs on a desktop Linux VM, one session; vendor trace and static WCET tools described, not demonstrated; example sizes not produced by a program are labeled assumed

findings.location: Section 4.1, output block of the wake-up runs (desktop-light-13, mobile-light-23)
findings.problem: Each 'absolute:' line is wider than the code box; at 1280 px it ends at 'jitter (max-mi', hiding the jitter and mean of every run, with no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: The section is about release jitter and the program's own jitter figure is hidden
findings.action: Print each run on two lines and re-run, or add a small table of the recorded values under the output
findings.acceptance: On new captures at 1280 px the jitter and mean of each run are readable without sideways scrolling

findings.location: Section 7, verification-workflow Mermaid flowchart (desktop-light-19 and 20, mobile-light-34)
findings.problem: The diagram has no caption saying what to notice (the loop back to the model when a bound is exceeded)
findings.whyItMatters: Minor; the numbered list repeats the cycle
findings.acceptance: facts.json of new captures reports 0 SVG figures without a title and the diagram has a caption

findings.location: Section 3.3 'tau_3‘s' (desktop-light-10, mobile-light-19); Section 6.1 and Exercise 3 grouped numbers (desktop-light-16 and 21, mobile-light-29 and 36)
findings.problem: A possessive after inline math renders as a left quotation mark, and grouped numbers (6 144, 7 372, 3 360 000) split across lines
findings.whyItMatters: Polish; a split number reads as two numbers
findings.action: Write ’ after the math; non-breaking spaces in grouped numbers, preferably by the site-wide step
findings.acceptance: None of the listed defects appears on new captures at 1280 or 360 px
